chunks: From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hasan Al-Lu'lu'i, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'If a servant upon whom Allah has bestowed a favor, either by being ill or tested with a calamity, and Allah cures him from that calamity, and he makes it upon himself to give up (a specific food or item) from Khorasan, then it is upon him to complete (his vow).'

key_terms.خُرَاسَانَ: Khorasan (a region, used here as an example of a specific item/type)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fulfilling a vow to abstain from a specific food or item after recovery from illness?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a vow of abstention (*ihram*) from a specific commodity, such as Khorasan wheat, becomes binding upon a person after they are cured of an illness or calamity. The ruling emphasizes the necessity of fulfilling the vow completely (*itmam*), reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle that voluntary vows create a binding obligation akin to debt, requiring full execution unless specific conditions for exemption are met.
